Contributing to calibrar

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for your interest in contributing to calibrar.

Contributions are welcome, including bug reports, questions, documentation improvements, examples, feature suggestions, and code contributions.

Reporting bugs

If you find a bug, please please open an issue.

When possible, please include:

  • a clear description of the problem;
  • a minimal reproducible example;
  • the version of calibrar you are using;
  • your R version and operating system;
  • any relevant error messages or warnings.

Suggesting improvements

Suggestions for improving the package, documentation, examples, or vignettes are welcome.

Please open an issue describing:

  • the motivation for the improvement;
  • the expected behaviour or output;
  • any relevant examples or use cases.

Contributing code

Code contributions can be made through pull requests.

Before submitting a pull request, please:

  • open an issue first if the change is substantial;
  • keep the proposed change focused;
  • follow the existing coding style of the package;
  • add or update documentation when relevant;
  • add or update examples or tests when appropriate;
  • check that the package can be built and checked successfully.

For R code, please use clear object names and keep functions as simple and focused as possible. Existing package conventions should be followed where possible.

Documentation

Documentation improvements are especially welcome. This includes corrections, clarifications, examples, vignettes, and improvements to function documentation.

For exported functions, documentation should be written using roxygen2 comments and should describe the purpose of the function, its arguments, return value, and relevant details.

Pull requests

When submitting a pull request, please include a short description of:

  • what the pull request changes;
  • why the change is useful;
  • whether it affects existing behaviour;
  • whether documentation or tests were updated.

Questions

Questions about using calibrar, interpreting outputs, or understanding the documentation can also be submitted as issues.

Code of conduct

Please keep discussions constructive, respectful, and focused on improving the package.

The calibrar package is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing to this project, you agree to abide by its terms.
